content.title: About
content.content: Wheat germ oil is a golden, nutty-smelling oil extracted from the germ of the wheat kernel, the embryo of the grain. It is one of the richest natural food sources of vitamin E. Wheat germ oil is used as a dietary supplement and as a flavorful finishing oil, and it is also used in skin and hair care products.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The wheat germ is the small embryo of the wheat kernel and makes up only a small fraction of its weight.
Wheat germ oil is among the richest natural sources of vitamin E.
It has a strong, nutty flavor and aroma.
It is sensitive to heat and light and is not suitable for frying.
Wheat germ oil is also used in cosmetics and skin care.

items.title: Very rich in vitamin E
items.content: Wheat germ oil is a concentrated source of vitamin E, an antioxidant that helps protect cells.

items.title: Provides polyunsaturated fats
items.content: It contains essential fatty acids, mainly linoleic acid, which the body needs.

items.title: Contains plant compounds
items.content: Wheat germ oil contains plant compounds such as octacosanol and phytosterols that are being studied.

items.title: Easy to add to foods
items.content: A small amount can be added to smoothies, yogurt, or dressings.

items.title: Used in skin care
items.content: Applied topically, it is used as a moisturizing oil.

items.title: Wheat allergy and gluten
items.content: Wheat germ oil is derived from wheat and may contain traces of wheat protein. People with wheat allergy or celiac disease should consult a healthcare professional before using it.

items.title: Possible medication interactions
items.content: High intakes of vitamin E may affect blood clotting. People taking blood thinners should consult a healthcare professional.

items.title: Rancidity
items.content: The oil spoils easily, and rancid oil should not be used.

items.title: Skin reactions
items.content: Applied to the skin, it may cause irritation or allergic reactions in some people. Do a patch test first.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Wheat germ oil is best used cold, drizzled over salads, stirred into smoothies, yogurt, or oatmeal, or used in dressings. Do not heat it or use it for frying, since heat damages its nutrients and flavor. Use only small amounts, since it is calorie-dense.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store wheat germ oil in a tightly closed dark bottle in the refrigerator after opening and keep it away from heat and light. Use it within the time given on the label. Discard oil that smells bitter, sharp, or like paint.
